bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices guide. No manufacturer manual exists for this model, so we built this from general best practices for this type of suppressor. It does not represent manufacturer data. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never disassemble a suppressor unless its maker documents it.
cleanIntro:
No maker procedure exists for the Otter Creek Labs Universe-36, so this guide treats it as a sealed can: nothing on it is opened, unscrewed or taken apart, whatever it looks like. Everything an owner can do safely is on the outside — take it off the host correctly, keep the mount and threads free of carbon, check that it is tight, look for the signs of trouble, store it dry, and know when it has to go back to Otter Creek Labs.

Listed in Fieldstrip as multi-calibre. The calibre rating marked on the can itself is the limit — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Host unloaded and the action open before the can moves
steps.action: Unload the host firearm, open the action and look: chamber empty, magazine out or empty. Keep the muzzle pointed somewhere safe the whole time the can is coming off — your hand is about to be in front of it.
steps.prose: This guide is for the suppressor, not the firearm. Clear the host the way the host's own manual describes.

steps.title: Let it cool before a bare hand goes near it
steps.action: A suppressor stays hot long after the barrel feels warm, hot enough to burn through an ordinary glove. Wait until it is cool to the touch, or handle it only in heat-resistant gloves, and set it down on something that cannot burn or melt.
steps.prose: ⛔ Never cool a hot can with water, solvent or compressed air.

steps.title: Off the host — and that is the whole strip
steps.action: Take it off the way it went on. On ordinary right-hand threads a can screwed straight onto the barrel turns counter-clockwise, seen from behind the gun, to come off. A quick-detach can releases its latch or collar first, then comes off the muzzle device. If carbon has it stuck, use steady hand pressure or a strap wrench on the tube — never pliers, a pipe wrench or a vice, which can crush the tube.
steps.prose: ⛔ Nothing else comes off. The mount, the end caps and whatever is inside stay exactly as they are: no procedure from Otter Creek Labs exists for this can, and a suppressor is never opened without its maker's. If it will not come off the host, stop and contact Otter Creek Labs.

steps.title: Carbon on the threads and the mount
steps.action: With the can off, look at the host's muzzle threads and shoulder, and at the threads or taper and the seating face of the can's mount. Hard carbon there is what stops a can seating square, and what makes one seize on or work loose. It comes off before the can goes back on — the cleaning list covers how.
steps.prose: The mount is the part of a suppressor that fails dangerously, so it gets the most attention.

steps.title: Look straight through it
steps.action: Hold the can up to a light and look through the bore from each end. You should see one clean, round circle of light, centred. Anything in the way — debris, water, a lip of metal, a torn or off-centre hole — means it does not go back on the gun.
steps.prose: Firing into an obstruction can wreck the can and injure the shooter.

steps.title: The outside of the tube
steps.action: Turn it in your hands and look for dents, bulges, cracks, a bent end cap or any burn-through. A dent can push the inside of the can into the bullet's path.
steps.prose: Damage you can see is a reason to stop and contact Otter Creek Labs, not to keep shooting it and see.

steps.title: Know the signs of a baffle strike
steps.action: A baffle strike is a bullet touching the inside of the can. The signs: the exit hole is torn, enlarged or off-centre; there are metal shavings or a bright fresh mark at the front; it suddenly sounds different; bullets start keyholing on the target. Any one of them puts the can out of service.
steps.prose: The usual causes are a can that was not seated square, a damaged or misaligned mount, or the wrong calibre through it.

steps.title: Listen for a new rattle
steps.action: Shake it gently by your ear. A new rattle, or anything you can feel shifting inside that did not before, means something has come loose. Do not fire it.
steps.prose: A faint sound from carbon flakes is common. Anything you can feel moving is a job for Otter Creek Labs.

steps.title: When it goes back to Otter Creek Labs
steps.action: Send it to Otter Creek Labs for inspection if: it shows any sign of a strike; it was fired with an obstruction in it or after a squib load; the tube is dented or cracked; it rattles; it will not come off the host or will not seat square, or the circle of light through it has visibly narrowed. Contact Otter Creek Labs before you ship it — they will tell you how to send a registered suppressor back legally.
steps.prose: For a can whose construction is unknown, the maker is the only way inside it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Otter Creek Labs Universe-36, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from Otter Creek Labs exists for this model, so nothing about how it is built inside can be known from a document — and a can whose construction is unknown is treated as sealed. Fouling inside it, a rattle, a strike, or a can that will not come off goes to Otter Creek Labs, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: MUZZLE THREADS & SHOULDER
tasks: Nylon or brass brush to break the carbon off the threads and the shoulder
Wipe with a cloth lightly dampened with gun solvent, then a dry cloth
Threads left clean and DRY — no oil, grease, anti-seize or thread-locker: whether this can wants any of them is a question for its maker, not something to guess

cleaning.name: THE CAN'S MOUNT — FROM THE OUTSIDE
tasks: Brush loose carbon off the mount's threads or taper and its seating face
A dry cloth over the mount face — nothing pushed into the can
⛔ The mount stays in the can: it does not come out

cleaning.name: QUICK-DETACH SEAT (if yours is QD)
tasks: Brush the taper or seat on the muzzle device — carbon on it stops the can locking up square
The latch or collar moves freely by hand; if it binds, stop and contact the maker

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE OF THE TUBE
tasks: Wiped down with a dry cloth
A can that got wet dries completely, standing on end, before it is stored or fired

cleaning.name: THE BORE — NOTHING THROUGH IT
tasks: ⛔ No patch, rod or bore brush through the can — a patch can lodge inside it
⛔ No soaking, no solvent fill, no ultrasonic bath: what this can is made of and how it is sealed is unknown, and either can damage it

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored off the host, clean and dry
Never shut in a case or bag while still damp
A thread protector back on the host's muzzle
Round count kept — the maker will ask for it if the can ever goes back

reassembly: Threads on the host and in the can clean and dry before it goes back on.
Start it by hand, square to the bore — it should spin on freely. If it binds or goes on crooked, back it off and start again; never force a cross-thread.
Run it down until it seats firmly against the shoulder or the muzzle device, with no gap you can see or catch a fingernail in. ⛔ A gap means it is not seated — do not fire.
Snug it firmly by hand, or with the wrench supplied with the can if it came with one. No cheater bar, and no tool on the tube that can crush it.
Quick-detach: latch or collar fully engaged, then pull and twist the can — it must not move.
Look through it once more before the first shot.
fncheck: Host still unloaded: the can is on, seated with no gap, and does not turn when you try it by hand. Check it again at the start of every session and after the first string of fire — a can that heats and cools can work loose. One that has loosened comes off, gets inspected and goes back on clean; one that keeps loosening goes to Otter Creek Labs.
